name: homebutler
description: Lets Claude read your server's status, Docker, backups and Proxmox, and what changed since the last saved report.
long_description:
HomeButler remembers what your server looked like at the last saved report and tells you, or Claude, what moved. The extension runs the homebutler binary on this computer as a local MCP server. It reads `~/.config/homebutler/config.yaml` when that file exists, and reaches the servers listed there over SSH.

It starts in read mode: Claude can look, and homebutler changes nothing. That includes saving report snapshots, so on its own the extension never reports a change: each report is a first look with nothing to compare. To get changes reported, save snapshots outside Claude by running `homebutler report` from an installed homebutler, by hand or from cron, or set **Highest tool risk** to `write`, which lets a report Claude runs save one.

`write` and `destructive` also offer the tools that change things, such as restarting a container, taking a backup or installing an app.

max_risk.title: Highest tool risk
max_risk.description: read, write or destructive. read: Claude can look and homebutler changes nothing. write: also tools that change something, such as restarting a container or taking a backup. destructive: also stopping containers, restoring backups and deleting app data.
